nodes.title: Scientific inquiry and evidence
nodes.mechanism: Science is deciding what counts as a fair question, an observation, and a model — not memorising labels.

nodes.title: What counts as a scientific question or test
Matter: materials, particles, mixtures and change
nodes.mechanism: Stuff is made of materials that can mix, separate, change state, or form new substances; the test is what stays the same and what is new.

nodes.title: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems
nodes.mechanism: Living things share life processes, live in habitats, and depend on food, microbes, and one another — health is not the absence of one symptom.

nodes.title: What is living; diversity and life cycles
Force, motion, magnets and pressure
nodes.mechanism: A push or pull between interacting objects changes motion; magnets and pressure are special cases of that interaction, not separate magic.

nodes.title: Energy, heat, electricity and light
nodes.mechanism: Heat, current, and light are ways energy and signals move; a circuit, a hot object, and a beam of light each need a complete path or medium.

nodes.title: Earth, sky, time and resources
nodes.mechanism: What we see in the sky and what we take from Earth are geometry plus materials: rotation, Moon phases, resources, and habitability — not myths about the Sun circling us.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: When deciding what counts as science, treat science as asking questions, observing, exploring, and doing things to understand the world, not as memorising facts alone.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Science is a way of thinking, observing, and doing things to understand the world; it begins with curiosity and questions about surroundings and continues through exploration.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Copying ten facts about the Sun from a chart is science because it has science facts.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: When trying to answer a question, choose the next step by moving from observation to question, from question to possible answer, and from possible answer to a test.
sample_hinges.mechanism: The scientific method is a step-by-step process: observe something interesting or unclear, form a question, guess a possible answer, and test the guess through further checking or investigation.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: The answer is that the ink is finished because the pen stopped writing.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: When observing an object, decide which substances are the materials it is made from.
sample_hinges.mechanism: A material is any substance used to create an object. Objects may be made from one material or from a combination of materials, and the same material can be used to make more than one kind of object.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: The material of the pen is pen.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: When grouping objects or materials, decide the common property being used for classification.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Classification means arranging objects into groups on the basis of a common property. Objects and materials can be classified by properties such as shape, colour, hardness, softness, shine, dullness, or the materials they are made from.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Glass tumbler, wooden board, and metal key belong in one group because all are things.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide whether an observed set of plants and animals represents biodiversity of a region.
sample_hinges.mechanism: The variety of plants and animals found in a particular region contributes to the biodiversity of that region, and each member can play a different role such as providing food or shelter or spreading seeds.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: The region with trees, birds, fish, and frogs is not evidence of biodiversity; biodiversity is what creates those different organisms.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Choose a valid basis for grouping plants or animals from their similarities and differences.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Plants and animals can be grouped on the basis of similarities and differences in their features, and different students may choose different common features for grouping.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Crow, ant, and cow form one useful group because they are all animals, with no common feature such as food, place, colour, or movement named.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide whether an object is made of a magnetic material by testing whether a magnet attracts it.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Materials attracted towards a magnet are magnetic materials; materials not attracted towards a magnet are non-magnetic materials. Iron, nickel, cobalt, and some of their combinations with other metals are magnetic.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Iron object: magnetic because it is metal; wooden pencil: non-magnetic because it is wood, without bringing the magnet near either object.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide where a magnet attracts magnetic materials most strongly.
sample_hinges.mechanism: A magnet does not attract magnetic materials equally at all parts; most iron filings stick near its two poles, and only a few stick to the remaining parts.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Only the North pole has maximum iron filings; the South pole has very few.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide whether a hot-or-cold judgement can rely on touch or must be checked by measuring temperature.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Sense of touch cannot always decide correctly whether a body is hot or cold; temperature is the reliable measure of hotness or coldness.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Container B is warm because my left hand feels it warm.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Use temperature readings to compare which body is hotter or colder.
sample_hinges.mechanism: A hotter body has a higher temperature than a colder body, and the difference in temperature tells how hot one body is compared with another.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: A cup at 25 °C is hotter than a cup at 40 °C because 25 is the lower reading.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide whether something should be called a natural resource by checking whether it is provided by nature and helps meet needs.
sample_hinges.mechanism: Resources required for survival are provided by nature. Resources provided by nature are called natural resources, and they sustain life and help make life more comfortable.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: Furniture is a natural resource because it is useful and makes life comfortable.

sample_hinges.decision_hinge: Decide why holding the breath becomes difficult and why oxygen in air is essential for survival.
sample_hinges.mechanism: The air we breathe in has oxygen. The body needs oxygen to perform its functions, so it is difficult to hold the breath for a long time and humans cannot survive without oxygen for even a few minutes.
sample_hinges.mx0_cwo: The body gives oxygen to the air during breath-holding, so holding the breath becomes difficult.
